All-New Mercedes AMG GT SUV Gets Rid of the Camouflage Ahead of the Impending Presentation - in CGI
28 photos
Photo: marianvalentincilibeanu / Instagram
The Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, the Ferrari Luce, or the Jaguar Type 01 – what do these models all have in common ? Quite a few things, actually…
All three of them are novel ultra-luxury and high-performance ‘sedan’ models with four doors. All three of them have more than 1,000 horsepower in their top configurations. All three of them have some naturally controversial design languages, both outside and inside. And, of course, all three of them are fully electric vehicles featuring new 800- or 850-volt dedicated architectures intended to remain relevant into the next decade.
Of course, all three of them have elicited very strong feelings across the Internet, with both specialists and amateurs discussing their new design languages. Funny enough, while all three of them are incredibly controversial, they’re also wildly different, showing that stylists now strive more than ever to stand out in any crowd, even though it may be the wrong one.
Anyway, there’s also one major detail that sets them apart: only one of them is going to receive a high-riding sibling before the end of the year. That’s going to be the Mercedes- AMG GT model, of course, which is getting the SUV option on October 17 at home in Stuttgart, with the Mercedes-AMG crossover built from scratch ready to anchor the fresh AMG.EA platform and showcase the direction of the brand’s future performance strategy.
There have been numerous reports, rumors, spied prototypes, and renderings – the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators are keeping very close to this one instead of dwelling aimlessly across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Now, here’s also Marian Valentin Cilibeanu, aka 'Cili' (known as marianvalentincilibeanu on social media), a Romanian virtual artist who also envisions the next Mercedes-AMG GT model in SUV form in a bid to get rid of the funky camouflage of the prototypes. Mercedes-AMG's first ground-up electric GT SUV model engineered entirely in-house might arrive at dealerships in early 2027, so it’s no wonder that everyone’s in a hurry to see it, by the way.
Mercedes-AMG’s first independently developed SUV, in these renderings, looks a bit less controversial than the GT 4-Door Coupe because now there are more vertical surfaces to play with, and the pixel master also deploys a trick – he mixes the larger three-pointed LED star daytime running lights with a full-width LED bar as if they’re a continuous element.
The front also has the new EV AMG grille on full display, now raised in a more elevated position compared to the GT 4-Door to allow new design elements to form the more classic front bumper. There’s just one CGI shot of the SUV going on a winding road, so we only catch a glimpse of the profile, and there’s no rear, but it’s pretty clear the AMG GT SUV will strive to remain practical as it prepares to fight the likes of the Bentley Torcal but also the Porsche Cayenne Electric, among other rivals.
